rows.citation: Oesterle J, Kraemer N, Hennig P, et al. (2022). Probabilistic solvers enable a straight-forward exploration of numerical uncertainty in neuroscience models. Journal of Computational Neuroscience 50:485-503.
rows.model_type: Single-compartment Hodgkin-Huxley, Izhikevich and STG neuron models, plus a three-neuron STG network (Python/Cython ODE implementations, not NeuroML).
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Models are not edited or faulted; variation comes from solver sampling, not model transformations.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Uses step, noisy step and pulse currents of varied amplitude and duration, but not as a designed protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - Measures spike times, spike counts, SPIKE-distance and trace errors; no eFEL-style feature fingerprint.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - No selection or minimisation of stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - Demonstrations on several models; no held-out model or mutation-family evaluation.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Quantifies numerical uncertainty in spike outputs, relevant to NeuroSem's tolerance calibration. NeuroSem would instead use step refinement to set tolerances for detecting model edits, adding mutation, protocol selection and held-out testing.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, abstract); Semantic Scholar API (PMC/PubMed IDs); PMC full text (methods); GitHub repository page.

rows.citation: Tomaiuolo M, Bertram R, Leng G, et al. (2012). Models of Electrical Activity: Calibration and Prediction Testing on the Same Cell. Biophysical Journal 103:2021-2032.
rows.model_type: Minimal conductance-based model of pituitary cell-line (GH4C1) electrical activity, fitted in real time with GPU plus dynamic clamp.
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - Predicts parameter changes that switch spiking and bursting, then tests them; not a systematic single-fault mutation set.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - Abstract describes recording and dynamic-clamp testing; number of distinct current-clamp protocols not stated in abstract.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - Distinguishes tonic spiking versus bursting patterns; standard feature library not indicated in abstract.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - No protocol battery selection described.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Calibrates on recordings, then tests model predictions on the same cell; a prediction test, not held-out models.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Fits models to living cells and checks predictions experimentally. NeuroSem compares a reference model with transformed versions in silico, using mutation-calibrated multi-protocol fingerprints and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); PubMed E-utilities efetch PMID 23199930 (authors, abstract); OpenAlex.

rows.citation: Abbas H, Hoxha B, Fainekos G, et al. (2014). Conformance Testing as Falsification for Cyber-Physical Systems. arXiv:1401.5200.
rows.model_type: Cyber-physical and hybrid dynamical system models (for example Simulink models and implementations); not neuroscience.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Compares models of differing fidelity or model versus implementation; no deliberate fault seeding reported in abstract.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Searches over input signals to expose non-conformance, rather than a fixed set of named protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - Uses trajectory distance measures, not electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - Falsification optimises inputs that maximise divergence; no compact battery chosen for coverage across faults.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - Case-study validation on several models; no held-out model or fault-family split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: General CPS analogue: searches for inputs exposing model divergence. NeuroSem is neuroscience-specific, uses interpretable electrophysiology features, mutation-calibrated batteries and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API for DOI 10.48550/arXiv.1401.5200; arXiv abstract page; Crossref for related WiP abstract 10.1109/iccps.2014.6843724 (ICCPS 2014, same six authors).

rows.citation: DeMillo RA, Lipton RJ, Sayward FG (1978). Hints on Test Data Selection: Help for the Practicing Programmer. Computer 11(4):34-41.
rows.model_type: General software programs; not neuron models.
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - Foundational mutation-testing paper; small seeded program changes used to judge test data adequacy.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Test data as sets of program inputs; no stimulation protocols.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - Concerns selecting test data that kills mutants; coupling effect suggests simple-fault tests catch complex faults.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - No held-out evaluation described in abstract.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Provides the mutation-adequacy and coupling-effect rationale NeuroSem borrows. NeuroSem applies it to neuron models with electrophysiology fingerprints, calibrated tolerances and held-out testing.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Papadakis M, Jia Y, Harman M, et al. (2015). Trivial Compiler Equivalence: A Large Scale Empirical Study of a Simple, Fast and Effective Equivalent Mutant Detection Technique. 2015 IEEE/ACM 37th IEEE International Conference on Software Engineering, pp. 936-946.
rows.model_type: C programs (6 large open-source plus 18 benchmark programs).
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - Generates program mutants and detects equivalent or duplicated ones via compiled binary comparison.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Equivalence judged statically from compiled output, not by running inputs.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Compared against hand-analysed equivalent mutants in benchmark programs.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Addresses equivalent mutants, which NeuroSem also faces when a mutation leaves behaviour unchanged. NeuroSem judges equivalence behaviourally, via tolerance-calibrated features, in neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, fourth author Yves Le Traon); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Tian Z, Shu H, Wang D, et al. (2024). Large Language Models for Equivalent Mutant Detection: How Far Are We? arXiv:2408.01760 (accepted at ISSTA 2024).
rows.model_type: Java methods (3,302 method-level mutant pairs).
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - Studies mutant pairs from mutation testing and classifies equivalence.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - LLMs judge code pairs; no execution protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Empirical evaluation of fine-tuned and prompted LLMs on a benchmark; not held-out mutation families.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - Uses LLMs to judge mutant equivalence, not to generate model transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses AI to detect equivalent software mutants. NeuroSem would check neuron-model edits, possibly AI-generated, by simulation under several protocols rather than code reasoning.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page (title, six authors, comment 'Accepted by ISSTA 2024', DOI).

rows.citation: Arcuri A, Briand L (2014). A Hitchhiker's guide to statistical tests for assessing randomized algorithms in software engineering. Software Testing, Verification and Reliability 24:219-250.
rows.model_type: Randomized software engineering algorithms (methodological guidelines).
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Statistical guidelines paper; no mutation method.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - None.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - Discusses evaluating randomized search algorithms, not proposing one.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - Statistical-test guidance, not held-out splits.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Methodological guidance NeuroSem could follow when comparing greedy against random batteries; not a competing method.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (issued online 2012-11-06; print volume 24, 2014); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Le V, Afshari M, Su Z (2014). Compiler validation via equivalence modulo inputs. Proceedings of the 35th ACM SIGPLAN Conference on Programming Language Design and Implementation (PLDI), pp. 216-226.
rows.model_type: C programs and optimizing compilers.
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - Creates program variants equivalent on given inputs by altering unexecuted code; semantics-preserving, not fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Relies on executing test inputs to define equivalence classes of program variants.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - Evaluated by bugs found in real compilers, not held-out splits.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Differential testing of transformations that should preserve behaviour on given inputs. NeuroSem targets neuron-model edits, measuring feature drift under several current-clamp protocols.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Lahiri SK, Hawblitzel C, Kawaguchi M, et al. (2012). SYMDIFF: A Language-Agnostic Semantic Diff Tool for Imperative Programs. Computer Aided Verification (CAV 2012), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, pp. 712-717.
rows.model_type: Imperative programs translated into the Boogie intermediate verification language.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Compares program versions; no seeded faults per available summary.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Static equivalence checking, not execution under inputs.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - Tool paper.
rows.software: SymDiff (named in paper; no repository URL verified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Formal semantic diff between program versions. NeuroSem gives an empirical, simulation-based behavioural diff for neuron models where formal equivalence is impractical.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, four authors); Semantic Scholar API (venue CAV, TLDR; abstract elided by publisher). Full text not read.

rows.citation: Deshmukh JV, Majumdar R, Prabhu VS (2017). Quantifying conformance using the Skorokhod metric. Formal Methods in System Design 50:168-206.
rows.model_type: Continuous and hybrid dynamical system models (for example Simulink) and their implementations.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Compares idealised models against implementations; no seeded faults per abstract.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Semi-formal approach simulates both systems over a large test set.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - Uses Skorokhod trajectory distance tolerant to timing distortion, not physiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - No compact test selection described in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None reported in abstract.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Offers a principled trajectory distance tolerant to timing shifts, an alternative to feature tolerances. NeuroSem adds neuron-specific features, mutation calibration and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Smith EK, Barr ET, Le Goues C, et al. (2015). Is the cure worse than the disease? Overfitting in automated program repair. Proceedings of the 2015 10th Joint Meeting on Foundations of Software Engineering (ESEC/FSE), pp. 532-543.
rows.model_type: C programs from a bug benchmark with human-written patches.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Evaluates automated repairs of real bugs, not seeded mutations.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Uses separate independent test suites beyond the repair tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: yes - Core design evaluates patches on tests independent of those used during repair.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - Automated repair tools (GenProg, TrpAutoRepair) transform programs; not LLM-based.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows edits passing one test set can break untested behaviour, which parallels NeuroSem's premise. NeuroSem applies this to neuron models with electrophysiology protocols and battery selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, fourth author Yuriy Brun); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Jimenez CE, Yang J, Wettig A, et al. (2023). SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues? arXiv:2310.06770 (published at ICLR 2024).
rows.model_type: Python repositories (2,294 GitHub issue tasks from 12 projects).
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Real issues, not seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Evaluated with repository unit tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Uses tests from the resolving pull request to judge model patches.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - Language models edit codebases to resolve issues.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Benchmark for LLM code edits judged by tests. NeuroSem concerns whether edits to neuron models preserve electrophysiological behaviour, with AI transformations only an optional case study.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page (title, seven authors, versions, comment citing ICLR 2024, DOI).

rows.citation: Li M, Yang X, Liu J, et al. (2026). A semantic mutation metric for metamorphic relation adequacy in scientific computing programs. arXiv:2605.17437.
rows.model_type: 12 single-output scientific computing programs (numeric, probabilistic, surrogate, machine-learning classes); not neuron models.
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - Five domain-semantic mutation operators (for example conservation erosion, hyperparameter changes), partly LLM-generated.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Metamorphic relations evaluated on transformed inputs; no current-clamp style protocols.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - Proposes an adequacy score for metamorphic relations; greedy selection not indicated in abstract.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - Abstract reports pre-registered effect-size tests; no held-out mutation family evident.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - LLM-generated semantic mutants compared with syntactic cosmic-ray mutants.
rows.software: Replication package on Zenodo (per arXiv comment; record URL not verified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest software-testing analogue: domain-semantic mutants to assess test adequacy in scientific code. NeuroSem targets NeuroML neuron models, electrophysiology fingerprints, tolerance calibration and compact protocol batteries.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page (title, four authors, v1 2026-05-17, v2 2026-07-07, comments, DOI). Full text not read.

rows.citation: Roache PJ (1994). Perspective: A Method for Uniform Reporting of Grid Refinement Studies. Journal of Fluids Engineering 116:405-413.
rows.model_type: Computational fluid dynamics discretisations.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - None.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - None.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Proposes the Grid Convergence Index from Richardson extrapolation, a precedent for refinement-based uncertainty. NeuroSem would adapt time-step refinement to set feature tolerances for neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, abstract).

rows.citation: Hansel D, Mato G, Meunier C, et al. (1998). On Numerical Simulations of Integrate-and-Fire Neural Networks. Neural Computation 10:467-483.
rows.model_type: Large networks of integrate-and-fire neurons.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - None.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Not indicated in abstract.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - Assesses network synchronization properties under different step sizes.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows time-step choice alters simulated neural dynamics, supporting NeuroSem's need for refinement-calibrated tolerances. No edit detection or protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, abstract).

rows.citation: Prinz AA, Bucher D, Marder E (2004). Similar network activity from disparate circuit parameters. Nature Neuroscience 7:1345-1352.
rows.model_type: Three-cell conductance-based model of the crustacean stomatogastric pyloric network.
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - Systematic parameter variation over 20 million model versions, a parameter-space database rather than single-fault edits.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Characterises spontaneous network output, not current-clamp protocols (per abstract).
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - Classifies network activity patterns by rhythm characteristics.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows different parameters give near-identical output, the degeneracy that makes some mutations look equivalent. NeuroSem tests whether other protocols expose such hidden changes.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); PubMed E-utilities efetch PMID 15558066 (abstract).

rows.citation: Gutenkunst RN, Waterfall JJ, Casey FP, et al. (2007). Universally Sloppy Parameter Sensitivities in Systems Biology Models. PLoS Computational Biology 3:e189.
rows.model_type: Collection of systems biology (biochemical network) models from the literature.
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - Analyses parameter-sensitivity spectra, not discrete single-fault edits.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Not electrophysiological stimulation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Tests sloppiness across many models; not held-out evaluation of a selected battery.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Explains why many parameter changes are behaviourally invisible. Background for NeuroSem's equivalent-mutant problem; no neuron models, protocols or detection framework.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, six authors); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Gerstner W, Naud R (2009). How Good Are Neuron Models? Science 326:379-380.
rows.model_type: Neuron models, from integrate-and-fire to conductance-based, evaluated in a spike-prediction competition (perspective article).
rows.controlled_mutations: no - None.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - Short perspective on a prediction competition; protocols not detailed in abstract.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - Judges models by spike-timing prediction quality.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Competition assessed prediction of recorded activity not used for fitting.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Discusses model quality against biological data. NeuroSem compares transformed models with their reference, which the spec lists as distinct from biological validation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, one-line abstract). Full text not read.

rows.citation: Van Geit W, De Schutter E, Achard P (2008). Automated neuron model optimization techniques: a review. Biological Cybernetics 99:241-251.
rows.model_type: Review of parameter fitting for computational neuron models.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Reviews parameter search, not fault seeding.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Reviewed fitness functions may combine responses, but stimulus batteries are not the focus of the abstract.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - Reviews feature-based error functions alongside trace comparison and multi-objective approaches.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - Optimises model parameters, not stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - Review article.
rows.software: Neurofitter (described in paper; URL not verified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Covers feature-based comparison for fitting models to data. NeuroSem reuses feature distances to detect edits and optimises the protocol battery, not parameters.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); PubMed E-utilities efetch PMID 19011918 (abstract).

rows.citation: Beck J, Deistler M, Bernaerts Y, et al. (2022). Efficient Identification of Informative Features in Simulation-Based Inference. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 35 (NeurIPS 2022), pp. 19260-19273.
rows.model_type: Single-compartment Hodgkin-Huxley model (Pospischil-derived, with M- and L-type currents) plus a toy model.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Parameters sampled from a prior for inference; no model edits.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - Paper text reviewed did not reveal multiple stimulation protocols; appears single-stimulus but unconfirmed.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - Ten summary statistics (spike counts, adaptation, ISI variability, resting potential) extracted with Allen SDK.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - Ranks informative features by posterior-uncertainty contribution; selects features, not stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - No held-out model or mutation-family evaluation evident.
rows.software: fslm_repo, https://github.com/berenslab/fslm_repo (URL from paper text; repository page not opened)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Identifies which electrophysiology features constrain parameters. NeuroSem selects stimulation protocols to detect model edits, with mutation calibration and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: arXiv abstract page and PDF text; Crossref /works for NeurIPS DOI 10.52202/068431-1400 (title, five authors, vol. 35, pages); NeurIPS proceedings page; Semantic Scholar API.

rows.citation: Davison AP, Brüderle D, Eppler J, et al. (2008). PyNN: a common interface for neuronal network simulators. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 2:11.
rows.model_type: Spiking neuronal network models run across NEURON, NEST, PCSIM, Brian and neuromorphic hardware.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - None.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Simulation interface; no protocol battery.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.software: PyNN (open source; URL not verified here)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Enables cross-simulator checking, which the spec treats as established. NeuroSem goes beyond one-script-many-simulators to mutation-calibrated behavioural testing of edited models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (lists only first author); PubMed E-utilities efetch PMID 19194529 (full eight-author list, abstract); OpenAlex. Article number 11 inferred from DOI suffix, not confirmed.

rows.citation: Pathmanathan P, Gray RA (2013). Ensuring reliability of safety-critical clinical applications of computational cardiac models. Frontiers in Physiology 4.
rows.model_type: Cardiac electrophysiology models (perspective on verification, validation and uncertainty quantification).
rows.controlled_mutations: no - None.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Discussion article.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - Discusses cardiac electrophysiology credibility, not feature fingerprints.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: General VVUQ framing for excitable-tissue models. NeuroSem offers a concrete verification-style method for neuron-model transformations; this paper proposes no such method.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Scharm M, Wolkenhauer O, Waltemath D (2016). An algorithm to detect and communicate the differences in computational models describing biological systems. Bioinformatics 32:563-570.
rows.model_type: SBML and CellML model versions in repositories such as BioModels and Physiome.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Detects differences between existing model versions; no seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - Structural and mathematical diff, no simulation.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.software: BiVeS (stated available from sems.uni-rostock.de; not opened)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Structural and mathematical diff of model encodings. NeuroSem asks whether such diffs change simulated behaviour, and which protocols reveal it, for NeuroML neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, abstract; issued online 2015-10-21, print volume 32 2016).

rows.citation: Glatard T, Lewis LB, Ferreira da Silva R, et al. (2015). Reproducibility of neuroimaging analyses across operating systems. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 9.
rows.model_type: Neuroimaging pipelines (FSL, Freesurfer, CIVET) across GNU/Linux versions; not neuron models.
rows.controlled_mutations: no - Varies operating system environment, not seeded model faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - Several analysis types and subjects, not stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - Imaging outputs (Dice, cortical thickness, ICA).
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows platform changes cause hidden output drift in neuroscience software. NeuroSem targets drift from edits to neuron models, detected with electrophysiology protocols.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata, 12 authors); OpenAlex (abstract).

rows.citation: Hook D, Kelly D (2009). Testing for trustworthiness in scientific software. 2009 ICSE Workshop on Software Engineering for Computational Science and Engineering (SECSE), pp. 59-64.
rows.model_type: Scientific computing software generally.
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - Concerns detecting code faults in scientific software; mutation use not explicit in abstract.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - None described.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - Suggests a small number of well-chosen tests can reveal many code faults.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - None reported in abstract.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Echoes NeuroSem's idea that a small well-chosen test set can catch many faults when oracles are lacking. NeuroSem makes this concrete for neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works (metadata); OpenAlex (abstract).
